questions.q: What was STELLARWIND, as described in the summary?
a: A US mass surveillance program created after 9/11
A Russian operation for monitoring dissidents
A global treaty meant to protect private data
A fund set up to reward government whistleblowers
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the US created STELLARWIND after 9/11, ostensibly for security but in practice to spy on citizens.

questions.q: What did Snowden do right after 9/11 to serve his country?
a: He joined the army but was sidelined by a broken ankle
He applied directly for a job at the NSA
He began studying law to defend civil liberties
He started a company building encryption tools
questions.why: Lesson 2 says he enlisted after 9/11, then left after a broken ankle and a few months of service.

questions.q: How was the leaked material eventually made public?
a: Through The Guardian, working with a filmmaker and a lawyer
Through a live interview Snowden gave on his own
Through documents mailed to members of Congress
Through a Russian outlet he approached first
questions.why: Lesson 2 says he worked with a filmmaker and a civil rights lawyer before giving the files to The Guardian.

questions.q: Where was Snowden stopped while traveling toward Ecuador?
a: Moscow, where he waited 40 nights at the airport
Berlin, where he waited for asylum papers
Hong Kong, where he hid in a hotel
Havana, where he was held for questioning
questions.why: Lesson 2 says he was stopped in Moscow and spent 40 nights in the airport before Russia granted him asylum.

questions.q: What does Snowden say he would need in order to return home?
a: A guarantee of a fair trial without the harshest penalties
A formal apology issued by the NSA
A presidential pardon granted in advance
A government job working on cyber defense
questions.why: Lesson 3 says he would come back if assured a fair trial and no death penalty or life without parole.
